column1: # The conformance matrix: one row per conformance point of the Federation Tier
# with AQL specification, section 17, in specification order, so that each
# executed test records the points it exercised (section 16.4, #41).
# Tab-separated; lines starting with # are comments.
# Derived columns, never edited by hand: cp, actor, requirements, tracks. They
# come from the vendored conformance.adoc through
# `scripts/checks/conformance-matrix.sh` fails when a fresh derivation differs.
#   covered       at least one test carries the point's marker and CI runs it
#   planned       no test yet; issue names the work (allowed until #89)
#   deferred      a Gateway point not scored yet; needs an issue and a reason
#   node-profile  a Node point, scored against the member CDRs in the harness, never the gateway (section 16.2)
#   operator      an Operator point, verified at admission or in the registry
# Deferral authority (no specification governs this: our own design): only the
# owner defers a Gateway point, by a decision recorded on the issue the row
# names. A session may propose a deferral on that issue and never applies one.
# The reason cites the specification's own optionality (MAY, provisional,
# section 18) or an open blocking issue.
# The marker on a test is one line directly above its #[test] or
# #[tokio::test] attribute, naming CP ids and tracks only:

column7: the status codes are scored (section 11.2, section 11.3); the OperationOutcome clause has no FHIR-facing consumer to apply to on an ITS-REST gateway, whose answer is a RESULT_SET with its additions under meta.federation only (N17, section 9.1, section 11.4)

section 12.3 and N22 route a version read on creating_system_id, while section 12a.1 route-ehr, section 12.5.1 and N41 route every request under a path ehr_id by that ehr_id; FerroFED follows N41, and the contradiction is recorded on #212

scored over two mock nodes: a versioned write naming its preceding version in If-Match, or in the path of a composition DELETE, reaches only the node its path ehr_id routes to, and only when the registry routes that version's creating_system_id there as the member's own system_id or a registered mapping; otherwise it is refused 409 and no node is sent it, a holder the map learned included; a versioned write naming no single version is refused 400; a new EHR with no target, or naming two endpoints, is refused 400 and never probed; a CONTRIBUTION is held to the same rule for every preceding_version_uid its body names, read with the ITS-REST NewContribution type and forwarded byte-identical, so one version another member controls refuses it 409 and no node is sent it, a CONTRIBUTION of creations alone routes by its path ehr_id, and a body that is no canonical-JSON CONTRIBUTION is refused 400

the stored-query clause is scored on a query stored at the gateway and invoked by name, targeted by the header and by the directive with the same answer, and refused 400 when the two select different node sets (section 8.4, section 12.7)

the routing clause is scored (explicit target, binding, index, then a read-only ask-all, and a write no earlier step routes refused 400 and never probed), and so is the integrity clause over two mock nodes: an ehr_id a binding, the index or the probe finds at two members is a 409 listing them on a read as on a write, neither is sent the request, one integrity incident is logged per refusal, and the index-insert alarm of section 12b.2 fires once; a binding collision is scored on the routing order alone until client sessions exist (#80), and the two-node harness of tracks 6 and 11 is #91
